newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Housing Bank fund to be launched soon.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Housing Bank fund to be launched soon.

text.p: Jordan's Housing Bank said on Wednesday it expected its 20 million dinar ($28 million) investment fund in mostly bluechip Jordanian stock to be launched within two months.
The fund, a wholly owned company of Housing Bank and managed by New York based Alliance Capital, will also focus on private equity and Jordanian debt instruments.

Bank officials told Reuters that the fund's final documentation papers were expected to be approved within a week to 10 days by the Bahraini Monetary Authority for listing on the Bahrain Stock Market.
Housing Bank's financial adviser, U.K.-based Clifford Chance, was now working with the Bahraini authorities in "approving the prospectus and the remaining documentation" one bank official said.
The fund is the first investment fund dedicated to Jordanian equities and debt instruments.
Bank officials chose to set it up in Bahrain to target Gulf and global investors, and because Jordan still has no legislation for establishing investment funds in Amman.
The bank plans to market it globally before formally launching it by May.
The three-year close ended investment fund will automatically become open-ended by the third year of the closing date of subscription, bank officials said.

The Jordan fund targets mainly foreign investors, high net worth individuals and Jordanian expatriates and has fixed an initial subscription price of 100 dinars per share with a minimum investment of ten shares.
The bank said the fund, which will be be listed on both the Amman bourse and the Bahrain Stock Exchange under a cross listing deal, aims also at attracting small investors.

Housing Bank, which has 121 branches across Jordan, is the main provider of private real estate credit but its commercial banking has long overtaken its original business and now ranks second among the country's banks in size of assets and deposits.
Housing Bank also plans, in line with foreign exchange liberalisation moves, to expand its investment and private banking business for its clients in capital markets.
